newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris stands by "kidnapping" of freed Basque chief.
newsitem.headline: Paris stands by "kidnapping" of freed Basque chief.

text.p: French Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre on Wednesday brushed aside accusations that the government broke the law by handing over a former Basque separatist leader to Spanish police after he completed a prison term in France.

A left-leaning magistrates' union denounced French police on Tuesday for allegedly kidnapping Josu Arkauz Arana of ETA, alias "Josu Mondragon", just before he was to leave the Fresnes prison near Paris.
"I assume responsibility for my action," Debre told reporters at a New Year reception, adding that he hoped French and Spanish police would boost cooperation in combating Basque violence.
"Natually, I hope that in 1997 this collaboration will continue, through the exchange of information and through police cooperation," Debre said.
Arkauz Arana, a leading member of ETA's military command, has been detained in French jails since 1991 and was wanted in Spain on a series of charges.
ETA has killed some 800 people in Spain during a three-decade-long campaign for a separate Basque state.
